items.text: The credits no longer mention the duck-rabbit at all. It is Dimitry's personal symbol, not a foundation.
The credits no longer call the duck-rabbit public domain. The idea of a duck-rabbit is; the icon in the index and on the cover is Dimitry's own hand-drawn mark, his trademark, and not open source.

Shape a held mark by dragging on it. With Hold on (the closed hand), tap a mark to hold it, then press on it and drag: up and down is its volume (a grey fill rises in the cell, with a bright line at the level), left and right is how much reverb that one note gets (a blue bar along the foot of the cell). A plain tap still lets the mark go, and dragging on marks that are not held still glides as before.

Held means sounding. A held place keeps its position, and what sounds is whatever mark is there now: when Weave (or a roll) puts a new mark under a held finger or Hold, the old sound lets go and the new mark sounds. A sound that cannot sustain (struck and one-shot sounds, like the drums) now repeats as a pulse, at half a beat, for as long as it is held.

Headings in the heads-up display are larger (much larger on a big screen), and each part (Field and marks, Look of the effects, Soniscale) starts with a divider, its icon and room above it. The field's explanation now sits right under its heading.

In full screen, a note you have held no longer stops the idle cinema from starting. Only a finger actually on the screen does. Before, a held mark counted as a finger for ever, so the interface never cleared.

When the app opens and the corner name is showing, the hand and field buttons wait at the foot of the right-hand column, just above the load meter, and slide up to the top right once the name has faded.
The Soniscale heading in Dice and air carries the load meter's icon.
The Off icon for the look of the effects is now a circle with a slash. (The old one, an archway, is kept in the handoff for something else.)

In Dice and air, "Touching" is now "Your finger plays" with the grid and field icons from the bar on its two buttons, and a line saying it only chooses which layer your finger plays and changes no slider. The mark-size slider says it sizes the grid's marks (the field's markers are not affected) and carries the grid icon; Floor pitch carries the field icon.

Every heads-up display pane now starts with the icon of the button that opened it, beside its name (the load meter's bars on Dice and air, the speaker on Mixer, the robot on Lines, the clock on Performance, the plug on MIDI, and so on), so you know you are where you pressed. Swipe to another pane and the icon follows.
Holding the sound-load meter now scrolls the Dice and air pane down to the Soniscale settings and flashes them, instead of opening at the top of a long pane.
